s1.syndrome_frame: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Grossly edematous glans penis and corona
Tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar and granulation tissue
Fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
key_facts: 78-year-old man
Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis of 1 month's duration
Asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis
Swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Routine blood test results were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, supports the diagnosis of a B-cell lymphoma. The fact that the lesion is localized to the skin and the patient has no prior history of lymphoma suggests a primary cutaneous origin. The large cell morphology and the expression of CD20 and CD79a are consistent with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The lymphoma cells are CD20+ and CD79a+, which are markers of B-cell origin, not T-cell or natural killer cell origin.

rejected.label: Mantle cell lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of cyclin D1 expression or t(11;14) translocation, which are characteristic of mantle cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The lymphoma cells are not confined to the blood vessels, and the clinical presentation is not consistent with intravascular lymphoma.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
rejected.why: The lymphoma cells have a large cell morphology, which is not typical of follicle center lymphoma, and the expression of CD5 is not consistent with follicle center lymphoma.

gold: Richter's transformation presenting as penile ulcer (transformation of chronic lymphocytic leukemia to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma)
